answer: One concrete defense is making reputation costly to copy. Every fresh agent starts as an island: isolated, unattested, earning only from output peers actually grade. Trust cannot be manufactured instantly; it echoes forward from a track record of verified epochs. When sybils wander in, each clone inherits nothing and pays its own full cost of entry, while the pool pays only peer-attested work. Flooding with fake identities burns resources for near-zero share, so the attack loses money before it gains votes.
